 Oral Order
Heard learned counsel for the Appellant and learned APP for the State.

2. This appeal has been preferred against the Judgment of Conviction dated 11.02.2022 and Order of Sentence dated 14.02.2022 passed by the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-VII-cum-Special Judge POCSO, Katihar in Case No G.R. 127 of 2020 arising out of Azam Nagar P.S. Case No. 08 of 2020, whereby the appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of POCSO Act and sentenced for the said offences.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-VII-cum-Special Judge POCSO, Katihar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned APP has not filed written objection despite having been given sufficient opportunities to her in this regard.
Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.1856 of 2022(6) dt.19-09-2023 4.

Learned counsel for the appellant presses the prayer for bail made by the appellant under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C.
5.

The main submissions advanced by the appellant's counsel are that the appellant, who is a very young person, has been undergoing in judicial custody since 04.05.2020 and he has spent more Md. Taushif vs The State Of Bihar on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99974128/
1 than three years in jail against the maximum sentence of rigorous imprisonment for ten years awarded upon him and there is no chance of early hearing of this appeal and so far as the merit of the instant matter is concerned, the so-called victim disclosed her age as eighteen years while recording her statement before Judicial Magistrate and before the Investigating Officer she disclosed her age as nineteen years, but as per Medical Board's opinion, her age was assessed between fifteen to seventeen years

entities.text: Md. Taushif vs The State Of Bihar on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
, hence, there is a serious contradiction in respect of the age of the victim and during trial, victim's school register purported to be of the victim's first attended school was produced but the same was not deemed reliable by the Trial Court and the allegation levelled against the appellant is completely false as the victim herself accepted her love affair with this appellant and in this regard relevant paragraph no. 13 of the impugned judgment may be perused.
6. Learned APP appearing for the State has opposed Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.1856 of 2022(6) dt.19-09-2023 the prayer for bail of the appellant.

7. Considering the above submissions and mainly the grounds taken by the appellant discussed above and also the custody period undergone by the appellant till date and also unlikelihood of appellant's appeal to be taken up for hearing in near future, this Court is inclined to accept the prayer for bail of the appellant made under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C.

Accordingly, let the appellant named-above be enlarged on bail during the pendency of this appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs.
10,000/- (ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Sessions Judge-VII-cum- Special Judge, POCSO, Katihar in Case No G.R. 127 of 2020 arising out of Azam Nagar P.S. Case No. 08 of 2020.
8.
